overview: A single turn-angle threshold helps decide which follow-up Transfigured Human A uses during a normal attack.
technicalOverview: Transfigured Human A (CN_120) has a deliberately small unique-data setup: one named row with a single meaningful tuning value. The character's action controller specializes ground and air NormalAttack_1, NormalAttack_3 and NormalAttack_3_1 actions, and the one traced unique value is a strict angle cut-off that decides whether an index-3 normal-attack branch changes to index 4 when the secondary target is missing or far off the facing. The other 13 slots are zero; no reachable CN_120 action, AI, effect, projectile, trap or shikigami reader was found for them. The descriptions below name reconstructed code by its observed behavior; row and float indices are zero-based and follow the supplied data.

CN_120.title: Single attack-targeting angle
CN_120.overview: This row supplies one secondary-target angle limit for CN_120 normal attacks. The remaining slots are zero, but zero is not treated as proof of disuse: they are listed as untraced after checking the character-specific and shared consumers.

0.label: Secondary-target angle limit
0.simple: Changes the normal-attack branch when there is no second target, or when that target is more than this many degrees away from where the character is facing.
0.technical: In TCN_120_NormalAttack_1<TBase>::GetAttackRow (used by both ground and air NormalAttack_1), the check runs only when the requested attack row Index is exactly 3. If a valid secondary target exists, the code takes that target's GAISlot014 location, subtracts the owner's GAISlot014 location, calls GetSafeNormal() on the 3-D delta, and compares AngleBetweenDegrees(owner facing forward, that direction) with unique(0,0). A strict '>' test remaps Index to 4; a target at exactly the stored angle does not remap, and indices other than 3 are untouched. With no valid secondary target, Index 3 remaps to 4 unconditionally. The traced unit is degrees; the supplied value is 90. A separate shared damage-reaction path, FGameCharacterAction_ProjectionSorceryReceive::Tick, uses unique(0,0) as RestraintTime only when Request.DamageTableRow is null; ActionElapsedTime accumulates DeltaTime and the reaction advances when that elapsed time reaches or exceeds the value. That fallback is not a CN_120-owned action.

notes.text: The row has no fallback sentinel or extra guard: the CN_120 read is a plain strict angle comparison, and only the missing-secondary-target case takes the unconditional branch.

Shared helpers that read other row-0 slots were checked but are not counted here. MakeUniqueCameraRequest reads slots 0-10 only when CameraMode is 2 and a caller supplies the row index; no CN_120 action calls it. The generic steering helper divides an angle by slot 0, and its only traced call sites are CN_041 and CN_140 action bodies, not CN_120.

Character setup resolves every Id_CharacterUnique name in order into UniqueRows, and the accessor is an unchecked UniqueRows[RowIndex]->FloatValue[ValueIndex] dereference. CN_120 has one populated entry in the supplied nine-entry list, so any dynamic row index above 0 would not select another CN_120 setting.

The only unique-float read in the CN_120 action TU is the NormalAttack_1 attack-row selection above. The shared notify-0 body for NormalAttack_3 and NormalAttack_3_1 instead sets a homing-invalidate timer from ActionStepRow->Step_HomingInvalidateDistance, resets inertia, and calls GAISlot186; it does not read this row.

UCN_120_ActionController creates only six specialized actions: ground and air NormalAttack_1, NormalAttack_3 and NormalAttack_3_1. Every other action type falls through to the shared base factory, so no other character-specific CN_120 action body was found that could read the remaining slots.

Two nearby combat quirks do not use the unique row: NormalAttack_3 plays StepR for a nonzero stick input whose flat camera-relative angle is greater than 45 degrees and less than 135 degrees with a positive cross product, and first-start NormalAttack_1 probes behind the owner (capsule radius plus 50) before resetting vector tweens when a level-facing wall or blocked follow-ground test is found.

Controller-level movement and social behavior are fixed rather than unique-row driven: NormalDash removes DashJumpBegin and adds RunJumpBegin to its cancel set; JumpAir and RunJumpAir add JumpAirBegin and RunJumpAirBegin; the controller allows two air jumps and refuses tag combo, revival buff and situation voice.

The AI type creates FGameCharacterAIThinkNode_CN_120. Its tick publishes only whether NormalAttack_3 or NormalAttack_3_1 is active, and its setup is the nine-slot normal-attack/movement set shared with CN_111 and CN_130. The timed hold executors that do read row-0 slots 0, 1 and 2 are selected by CP_040's behavior controller, so their duration reads are not assigned to CN_120.

Delegated unique-float paths were kept separate: trap actions forward GetUniqueFloat to the spawner's source interface, returning 0 when there is no source, while AGameShikigami's same-named accessor indexes its own UniqueRows from ShikigamiUniqueDataTable. Neither is a read of this AGameCharacter row.
